Suppose $Y$ is a continuous random variable. We wish to conduct a chi-square goodness-of-fit test at the $1%$ significance level with the following null and alternative hypotheses:

- $H_{0}$: $Y∼N(10, (\sqrt{10})^{2})$
- $H_{1}$: $Y≁N(10, (\sqrt{10})^{2})$

A random sample is carried out, and the sample data is shown below. The rightmost column gives $P(a < Y < b)$ under the null hypothesis, where $a$ and $b$ are the boundaries for each class of observations.

| Observations $(y_{i})$ | Frequency $(O_{i})$ | $P(a < Y < b)$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| $0 \le y_{i} < 4$ | $8$ | $0.0281$ |
| $4 \le y_{i} < 8$ | $34$ | $0.2347$ |
| $8 \le y_{i} < 12$ | $99$ | $0.4729$ |
| $12 \le y_{i} < 16$ | $29$ | $0.2347$ |
| $16 \le y_{i} < 20$ | $10$ | $0.0281$ |

The table below gives the values of $w$ that satisfy $P(W \ge w) = p$, where $W∼χ^{2}(ν)$.

| $ν∖p$ | $0.100$ | $0.050$ | $0.025$ | $0.010$ | $0.005$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $3$ | $6.251$ | $7.815$ | $9.348$ | $11.345$ | $12.838$ |
| $4$ | $7.779$ | $9.488$ | $11.143$ | $13.277$ | $14.860$ |
| $5$ | $9.236$ | $11.070$ | $12.832$ | $15.086$ | $16.750$ |

Using this information, select the options that make the following statements true.

Rounded to one decimal place, the test statistic is
{{field-1}}.

The number of degrees of freedom for this test is $ν =$ {{field-2}}.

At the $1%$ significance level, there is {{field-3}} evidence to reject the null hypothesis.
